segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Mira and Tomas were two when I discovered twelve adults were easier to negotiate with than either of them.

Not together.

Individually.

Together they formed a labor action.

That morning the dispute was trousers.

Tomas did not want his.

Mira wanted his because they had a blue tie.

Her trousers also had a blue tie.

This did not matter.

"Mine," Tomas said.

He was holding neither pair.

"Yours," I agreed.

"No."

There it was.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Tomas had expanded his vocabulary since fourteen months.

He still preferred the classics.

Mira had taken the opposite approach.

She had too many words and used all of them.

"Why his blue?"

"Because those are his trousers."

"Why?"

"Because they fit him."

"Mine fit."

"Correct."

"Why?"

I looked at Nessa.

She was fastening her district coat.

Coward.

"You made them," I said.

"I contributed."

"You are leaving."

"I have a transfer meeting."

"I have trousers."

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
She kissed Mira's head.

Mira said, "Why?"

Nessa kissed Tomas too.

He wiped his forehead.

Cruel child.

Then she kissed me.

I did not wipe anything.

Evidence of maturity.

"Your sleeve," she said.

I looked.

Porridge.

Dry already.

I rubbed at it.

Worse.

"Leave it," Nessa said.

"I have district later."

"Then they will know you ate."

"Professional."

"Very."

She left.

I got both children dressed eventually.

Not in the original trousers.

Important distinction.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
My mother arrived before midday.

Also important.

I had just started pretending the morning was under control when a district runner knocked.

WEST THREE.

STAFFING DISPUTE.

HALDEN REQUESTS YOU.

I read it twice.

Mira stood on my foot.

"What says?"

"Work."

"Why?"

"Because apparently people there are arguing."

"Why?"

"That is what I am going to find out."

She considered this.

"Why?"

I looked at my mother.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
She smiled with the satisfaction of someone whose difficult children had become someone else's difficult children.

I left with porridge still on my sleeve.

West Three had lost two experienced operators in the same month.

One retired.

One moved south because his wife's family owned a house there and rent is stronger than loyalty.

The station filled the gaps with overtime.

Reasonable for a week.

Then three.

Then seven.

People began making mistakes.

Not disasters.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Wrong log entries.

Missed lubrication.

One valve tagged on the wrong side.

A night operator fell asleep during a quiet hour and woke before anything noticed.

That last part became a joke.

It should not have.

The crew asked district for temporary hires and an overtime cap.

District approved one temporary hire.

No cap.

West Three's crew refused voluntary overtime after the next schedule.

District called it a staffing action.

The crew called it sleeping.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Both descriptions were accurate.

The problem was West Three could not run nights on its normal roster without somebody staying extra.

So district sent two Authority Rankers as temporary hazard coverage.

Strong people.

Good field records.

One B-class.

One high C.

Neither had operated West Three.

They arrived with the confidence of men told they were the solution.

That is rarely their fault at first.

The station foreman, Iven, showed them the lower controls.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
The B-class man asked, "Where is the automatic transfer?"

Iven said, "There isn't one."

"Manual?"

"Yes."

"How often?"

"Depends."

"On?"

"Everything."

The Ranker did not enjoy that answer.

By second night, West Three had missed two low-load adjustments and overfed the west return enough to wake a whole apartment line with pipe hammer.

Nobody hurt.

Thirty complaints.

That was when Halden sent for me.

Coward.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
I arrived at a meeting with twelve people and no chairs arranged correctly.

Bad start.

West Three crew on one side.

Authority Rankers on the other.

District payroll clerk in the middle looking like she regretted education.

Iven near the wall.

Tess Mor, crew representative, had three schedules in front of her and the expression of someone prepared to use all of them as weapons.

I moved one chair sideways and sat.

The B-class Ranker looked at me.

"You mediation?"

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
"No."

"Then why are you here?"

"Halden hates me."

That was not useful.

The payroll clerk said, "Gregory has station and district authority."

"Greg."

She ignored me.

"His role is technical facilitation."

I looked at her.

"That means mediation."

"Only if it works."

Good clerk.

Tess started first.

"We are done with voluntary nights."

The payroll clerk said, "Voluntary extended nights."

Tess looked at her.

"Those are the nights we mean."
